title: Sum of Powers: Extension to Non-Integer Exponents
description: Extends Faulhaber's formulas to real exponents via the p-series ζ(s) = ∑ 1/n^s. Proves convergence dichotomy (iff s > 1), recovers ζ(2) = π²/6 and ζ(4) = π⁴/90, establishes term and zeta monotonicity, and bridges real-exponent theory to integer power sums.

sections.title: Convergence Dichotomy
sections.description: The p-series ∑ 1/n^s converges if and only if s > 1.

sections.title: Known Values
sections.description: ζ(2) = π²/6 (Basel Problem) and ζ(4) = π⁴/90.

sections.title: Term and Zeta Monotonicity
sections.description: Each term 1/n^s decreases in s for n ≥ 1, so ζ(s) is antitone.

sections.title: Bounds
sections.description: ζ(s) ≥ 1 and ζ(s) ≤ π²/6 for s ≥ 2.

sections.title: Bridge to Integer Exponents
sections.description: Connects real-exponent rpow series to classical 1/n^k via rpow_natCast.

overview.text: Faulhaber's formulas give ∑ k^m for integer m. The natural extension to real exponents s leads to the p-series ∑ 1/n^s, whose limit is the Riemann zeta function. This formalization proves the convergence dichotomy at s = 1, recovers the Basel Problem value, and establishes monotonicity and bounds.
keyInsights: The p-series convergence threshold at s = 1 separates convergent from divergent behavior
Known zeta values connect discrete sums to transcendental constants (π)
Monotonicity in the exponent follows from rpow monotonicity via inversion
The bridge theorem rpow_inv_eq_nat_inv connects real and integer exponent theories

conclusion.text: This formalization provides the analytical foundation for extending Faulhaber's discrete power sums to continuous exponents. With 11 of 14 results fully proved and 3 sorries (tsum ordering comparisons), the key mathematical content is captured.

crossReferences.description: Extends integer power sums to real exponents
Uses ζ(2) = π²/6 for upper bounds and known values
